reasons: The explicit expression-source/1 profile and separate entry points provide an appropriate bounded component toward the requested compact TypeScript-style DSL.
Profile-gated productions preserve syntax/0, atomic/1 and funded-source/0 semantics without an implicit upgrade.

Complete nominal and numeric metadata, exact type equality, signed literal forms and rejection without normalization preserve the runtime type model.
The proposal now specifies unit pairing, eight-unit limits, exponent and scale domains, unsigned Price mantissas, distinct Price assets, collection capacities and exclusion of Unit data values.
The explicit source nesting and lexical restrictions appropriately limit representability; unlimited Core metadata preimages are not required.
All 40 constructor names have mappings with the required operand roles. Operators and constructors remain composable within the simultaneous source and Core bounds.
Collection construction now admits 128 operands, and direct emit O expression preserves arbitrary Record-valued operands without inserting a replacement constructor.
Fixed generic-primary exclusion, bracket punctuation, metadata forms and projection-resolution order address the earlier parsing and namespace gaps.
Lexical operand order, access aliases and the two-node lowering of != preserve the specified Core structure and work accounting.
This vote covers constructor mappings and accepted syntax. The conflicting rejection rule for operation type arguments requires the D5 correction below.
Immutable trusted schema text and fresh, owned JSON trees prevent evaluation requests or previous returned objects from reclassifying fields or changing subsequent evaluations.
The 256-parameter limit matches the aggregate schema declaration ceiling while retaining simultaneous byte, token and schema bounds.
Optional declarations now have concrete membership checks. Name-only asset declarations avoid inventing an asset/denomination relation absent from Sigma.
Exactly one intrinsically selected action avoids an unsupported host action registry.
The component explicitly leaves complete agreement declarations, financial transitions and full SP02 open. ExpressionPrepared does not establish Midnight execution or financial acceptance.
The seven-phase structure substantially improves admission ordering, whole-action static checking, typed snapshot validation and reduction boundaries.
VALUE_BOUND and DESCRIPTOR_BOUND, inserted-node spans, Core child paths, rollback and conservative work B are now specified.
The closed diagnostic catalog promises phase-4 SOURCE_OPERATION when emission type arguments are supplied, but the replacement emission grammar cannot parse that form.

Phase 1 requires a finite snapshot-envelope byte gate without defining its ceiling or explicitly inheriting the baseline transport ceiling. Implementers can therefore choose different admission boundaries and error precedence.

requiredCorrections.finding: The grammar and closed diagnostic catalog disagree about operation type arguments.
requiredCorrections.witness: With O registered, emit O<UInt64> {}; cannot pass the replacement emission production: after identifier O, neither the braced alternative nor expression can begin with '<'. It therefore fails phase 2, although line 284 promises phase-4 SOURCE_OPERATION for supplied type arguments.
requiredCorrections.correction: Choose one contract explicitly: retain identifier-only emission and specify the parser rejection, or admit a syntactic operation type annotation and reject its arguments during elaboration. Align grammar, AST expectations, catalog and precedence examples.
requiredCorrections.evidenceClass: Static derivation from exact proposal bytes; no candidate parser execution.

requiredCorrections.finding: The new snapshot transport requires a finite envelope byte limit but does not state its value.
requiredCorrections.witness: The baseline runtime explicitly uses a 2000000-byte transport ceiling for its different request object. Proposal 02 defines a new four-key snapshot object and independent 65536-byte snapshots, but does not select an outer limit. Applying 65536 to the whole envelope would incorrectly reject independently admissible components.
requiredCorrections.correction: State the exact outer transport ceiling and its error/precedence before JSON parsing, while preserving each independent snapshot ceiling. A derived safe ceiling for the specified canonical object is 196653 bytes: three 65536-byte components plus 45 bytes of keys, punctuation and maximum-width workInitial. Alternatively, explicitly retain a sufficiently large existing transport ceiling.

limits: This is one independent design review of proposal 02 only. It supplies no second-reviewer vote, consensus or implementation approval.

No delegation, edits, builds, candidate parser/runtime tests, financial operations, proof campaigns, service calls, network acquisition or private-data access occurred. The mandated guarded status command was attempted and failed.
Grammar witnesses are static derivations, not reproduced implementation failures.

All40 means constructor, operand and composition fidelity within simultaneous source byte/token/depth/name and Core bounds; it does not require unlimited Core preimages or a complete agreement frontend.
Real-source coverage, formatter round trips, boundary admission, error precedence, spans, work, ownership and rollback remain specified-only until checked against frozen implementation bytes.

Full SP02, static semantics, K correspondence, financial-operation semantics, ACTUS/DeFi coverage, mandatory PCD and Preview acceptance remain mandatory and open. ExpressionPrepared satisfies none of those product acceptance gates by itself.
